events.title: Battle of Trafalgar
events.description: A British Royal Navy fleet commanded by Vice-Admiral Horatio Nelson decisively defeated the combined French and Spanish fleets off the coast of Spain near Cape Trafalgar. Nelson was mortally wounded by a sniper during the battle and died shortly before its conclusion.
events.significance: The victory cemented British naval supremacy for over a century and ended Napoleon's hopes of invading Britain by sea.

events.title: Thomas Edison Demonstrates a Practical Incandescent Light Bulb
events.description: At his laboratory in Menlo Park, New Jersey, Thomas Edison and his team successfully tested a carbon-filament incandescent lamp that burned for about 13.5 hours, and later for much longer with refinements.
events.significance: This breakthrough led to commercially viable electric lighting and helped usher in the age of widespread electrification.

events.title: Birth of Alfred Nobel
events.description: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist, engineer, and inventor, was born in Stockholm. He invented dynamite in 1867 and amassed a large fortune through his industrial enterprises.
events.significance: Nobel's will established the Nobel Prizes, which have become the most prestigious international awards in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, and peace.

events.title: Guggenheim Museum Opens in New York City
events.description: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, designed by architect Frank Lloyd Wright, opened to the public on Fifth Avenue in Manhattan. Its distinctive spiraling, inverted-ziggurat design was radical for its time.
events.significance: The building became an icon of modern architecture and reshaped ideas about how museums could be designed and how art could be displayed.

events.title: Aberfan Disaster
events.description: A colliery spoil tip collapsed and slid onto the Welsh village of Aberfan, engulfing Pantglas Junior School and nearby houses. 144 people died, including 116 children.
events.significance: The tragedy prompted major reforms in mining safety and regulation of waste tips in Britain and led to inquiries that criticized the National Coal Board for negligence.
